subject: Vocabulary
topic: Word Roots — Greek and Latin Origins (Set W7)

questions.stem: The root 'BENE' (as in 'benefit', 'benevolent', 'benefactor') comes from Latin and means:
questions.explanation: B is correct. BENE (Latin) = good/well. Benefit = advantage (good thing). Benevolent = wishing good to others. Benefactor = one who does good deeds. Contrast: MALE/MALI = bad (malevolent, malicious, malefactor).

B is correct. DEMOS (Greek) = people. Democracy = rule by the people. Demography = study of the people/population. Epidemic = upon (epi) the people — a disease affecting many. Contrast: GEO = earth; KRATOS = power; THEOS = god.

C is correct. OMNI (Latin) = all/every. Omnipresent = present everywhere. Omnivore = eats everything (plants + animals). Omniscient = knowing everything (sci = know). Contrast: SEMI = half; NULL = nothing.

questions.stem: The root 'CHRON' (as in 'chronology', 'chronicle', 'synchronise') comes from Greek and means:
questions.explanation: A is correct. CHRON (Greek: chronos = time). Chronology = study of time/sequence of events. Chronicle = historical record in time order. Synchronise = make happen at the same time (syn = same + chron = time). Contrast: PHON = sound; MNEMO = memory; BIO = life.

D is correct. TERR (Latin: terra = earth/land). Terrestrial = of or relating to the earth. Territory = a tract of land. Terrain = land features. The Mediterranean Sea name means 'middle (medius) of the earth'. Contrast: AQUA = water; AER = air; PYRO = fire.

A is correct. GRAPH (Greek: graphein = to write/draw). Photography = writing/drawing with light. Biography = life (bio) writing. Paragraph = section of writing. Contrast: SCOP/OPTIC = see; LOG/LOQ = speak; METR = measure.

questions.stem: The root 'MORT' (as in 'mortal', 'mortgage', 'post-mortem') comes from Latin meaning:
questions.explanation: C is correct. MORT (Latin: mors/mortis = death). Mortal = subject to death. Post-mortem = after (post) death — examination of a body. Mortgage = literally 'dead pledge' (mort + gage) — a debt cancelled only by death or completion. Contrast: VITA/BIO = life; NAT = birth.

questions.stem: The root 'PATH' (as in 'pathology', 'sympathy', 'apathy') from Greek means:
questions.explanation: B is correct. PATH (Greek: pathos = disease/suffering/feeling). Pathology = study of disease. Sympathy = feeling with someone (syn = with + pathos = feeling). Apathy = without feeling (a = without). Empathy = feeling into another's emotions. Note: PATH as 'way' is a different English word (from Old English 'paed') — do not confuse with the Greek root.

A is correct. CRED (Latin: credere = to believe/trust). Credible = believable. Incredible = not believable (in = not). Credential = evidence supporting someone's credibility. Credit = trust extended (in financial sense). Creed = a statement of belief. Contrast: CREATE = to make; JUDIC = to judge; DONO = to give.

questions.stem: Identify the word whose root does NOT share the meaning 'light' with its family: 'illuminate', 'luminous', 'luna', 'illustrate'.
questions.explanation: D is correct. ILLUMINATE = to light up (lumen = light). LUMINOUS = giving off light. LUNA = moon (Roman moon goddess, moon reflects light — from 'lux' light family). ILLUSTRATE comes from Latin 'illustrare' but its root 'lus/lust' means 'to make bright/clear' in the sense of clarity, not physical light. In modern usage 'illustrate' means to make clear through pictures — it has drifted from the light-family. Among the options, 'illustrate' is the most removed from 'light' in practical meaning.
